# Shellport

> A personal web terminal with saved SSH targets, optional terminals on its hosting computer and tmux sessions that can be resumed across devices. A Go server embeds the web interface; phones connect through a browser.

When asked to install Shellport, read INSTALL.md first. Discover the actual computer and the user's intended access, propose a concrete setup, and obtain confirmation before downloading, building, installing or changing services, networking or credentials. An installation request alone should not decide those choices for the user. Continue within the confirmed plan without asking again for every routine step.

Choose a release for the hosting computer's OS and userspace architecture, not the phone. Supported release targets are Linux amd64, arm64 and ARMv7, plus macOS arm64 and amd64. Prefer a verified stable release. If none is published or no compatible asset exists, propose building the embedded interface and server from trusted source. Do not interpret network or authentication failures as proof that releases are absent.

Shellport binds to loopback. Device access needs a reachable hostname, trusted HTTPS proxy with WebSocket support on the same computer, matching allowed origins and a private access boundary. Preserve existing installations and keep persistent data outside executable release directories. Enable local shells only with the user's agreement. Never print or upload private keys or passwords.

For new local terminals, independent tmux is the default: init --local-shell previews and confirms an isolated Linux systemd user service or macOS launchd user agent. Managed mode (--tmux-mode managed) needs no OS service and ends its local tmux shells when Shellport stops. Both modes create sessions/tabs through the interface. Discuss that difference during the installation plan. Use --dry-run to inspect service paths and startup requirements before --yes for an already approved unattended setup. Install tmux first; service setup does not install OS packages or enable user lingering. These choices do not change SSH targets.

Existing configurations retain their prior tmux behavior. Stop Shellport before setup-tmux; never kill saved work to make a mode change pass. Preserve custom wrappers and services, private backups and installation credentials. New configurations use a dedicated socket; shellport tmux --data-dir PATH -- <tmux arguments> connects another client to it. Read INSTALL.md for migration and rollback limits.

Discuss local privilege policy separately from session lifetime. Direct and managed local shells inherit Shellport's process restrictions; independent tmux has its own service policy. For a new independent Linux service, --tmux-privileges account uses the account's normal OS rules, while restricted blocks setuid privilege elevation with NoNewPrivileges=true. Omission preserves an existing owned policy, or uses account for a new service. Preview with --dry-run. Do not relax existing supervisor policies, edit external services or .tmux.conf, grant root/passwordless sudo, or restart tmux without an agreed plan. Existing processes retain their restrictions; policy changes cannot migrate live shells. Settings reports this Linux process flag read-only, not overall sudo availability, and returns Unknown when detection is unreliable. Read INSTALL.md's Local shell privileges section before changing an existing setup.

Both local modes can coexist. Workspace settings → Local sessions shows their counts, enables the other pool after confirmation and sets the default for new sessions. Existing work keeps its server, mode and stable reference. New tabs inherit the selected session’s mode. The picker's collapsed Advanced section contains the Session lifetime toggle when both pools are configured and explains both modes. Open direct shell sits below Create and connect and opens a normal shell from the same saved computer. Direct shells end on disconnect and do not change Continue. Add/Edit computer has no persistence checkbox; tmux availability is discovered when connecting. A confirmed missing tmux executable makes direct shell the primary action. Network, identity, authentication, permission and execution failures remain explicit errors; do not silently reinterpret them as missing software or install anything automatically. Enabling independent mode creates a separate user service; managed mode remains owned by Shellport. Preserve tmuxAdditional in the private config, do not move running processes between sockets, and do not rewrite the operator’s original wrapper or service. The CLI tmux client accepts --tmux-mode to select a configured pool explicitly.

Login offers passkeys with an app-password fallback. Agree on a stable HTTPS hostname before the user enrolls a passkey; each hostname has separate credentials. Back up passkeys.json with the rest of the private data directory. The user must complete passkey enrollment and their device's confirmation prompt themselves.

This file is an entry point for assistants; it is not executable and does not automatically configure a machine. The personal setup example is optional, not a default to reproduce.

## Installation and operation

- [Installation guide](INSTALL.md): Discovery, confirmation, release selection and verification, source builds, configuration and acceptance checks.
- [README](README.md): Current commands, networking requirements, browser use, offline password recovery and session behavior.
- [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md): Release notes and compatibility limits. Use `shellport version` to identify an installed binary.
- [Backup and recovery](BACKUP.md): Consistent backups, executable upgrades, rollback, restoration and the disposable rehearsal.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/tauki/shellport): Inspect the selected version's source and build requirements.
- [GitHub releases](https://github.com/tauki/shellport/releases): Find an explicit tag and matching server archive when releases are available.

## Optional

- [How I use it](HOWIUSEIT.md): The author's hosting, private network and phone setup; none of its named infrastructure is required.
